title: Renewal Risk Ladder Playbook
content:
Overview

Purpose: Introduce the "Risk Ladder"—a tiered, time-bound escalation and mitigation framework to standardize how CSMs, AMs, and Execs identify, triage, and save at-risk renewals. The ladder creates crisp thresholds, play types, and owner handoffs so that interventions happen early, consistently, and with executive visibility when needed.

Why a ladder? Teams frequently miss subtle early signs and then scramble late. The Risk Ladder converts signal thresholds into repeatable actions and a clear escalation timeline (rungs = response windows).

Risk Ladder: levels and triggers

- Level 0 — Stable (Green)
  - Trigger: Renewal health score >= 85, active usage, no open P1/P2s.
  - Actions: Standard QBR cadence, share roadmap, light-touch adoption nudges. Owner: CSM.

- Level 1 — Watch (Yellow) — 90–120 days before renewal
  - Trigger: Health score 65–84 OR decline in weekly MAU >10% OR adoption stalled on key modules.
  - Actions: 2-week action sprint: usage audit, customer success plan refresh, schedule an "adoption jumpstart" workshop. Assign runbook tasks and owner. Owner: CSM + Solutions Eng.

- Level 2 — Concern (Orange) — 60–90 days before renewal
  - Trigger: Health score 45–64 OR unmet milestone in rollout OR at least one high-impact bug unresolved >7 days.
  - Actions: Create a triage ticket, escalate to SE to produce remediation ETA, propose a commercial safety net (credit/discount + conditional extension), invite Sales AM. 48-hour check-in cadence. Owner: CSM + AM + SE.

- Level 3 — Critical (Red) — 0–60 days before renewal
  - Trigger: Health score <45 OR expressed intent to not renew OR multiple executive complaints OR legal/contract issues.
  - Actions: Immediate escalation to Escalation Lead and Exec Sponsor. Assemble "Save Squad" (CSM, AM, Solutions Eng, Product PM, Legal, Finance). Run 72-hour rapid-response plan with daily exec brief. Prepare a focused remediation roadmap and commercial proposal. Owner: Escalation Lead + Exec Sponsor.

Escalation thresholds and timelines

- Automatic executive alert: any Level 3 box checked or 2+ Level 2 triggers sustained for >14 days.
- Escalation windows: each ladder rung has a prescriptive window for next-step confirmation (e.g., Level 2 -> Level 3 must be decided within 72 hours).
- Decision gates: after 5 business days of Level 3 remediation without clear forward motion, recommend either (A) an executive intervention call with customer C-suite or (B) contract transition planning with Sales Ops.

Roles and responsibilities

- CSM: primary owner for monitoring health score, executing Level 1 plays, and maintaining the renewal runbook.
- Solutions Engineer (SE): technical triage, fixes, and estimated delivery dates.
- Account Manager (AM): commercial proposals, concessions, and contract negotiation.
- Escalation Lead: operational coordinator for Level 3; runs Save Squad and daily exec briefs.
- Exec Sponsor: provides access to executive-level commitments (roadmap priority, approved concessions).
- Legal & Finance: enable quick contract addenda and pricing approvals.

Play types and example interventions

- Adoption Jumpstart (Level 1): 60–90 minute workshop, tailored success plan, prioritized feature enablement checklist, 30-day usage goals.
- Technical Hotfix Sprint (Level 2): SE-led 2-week sprint with prioritized bug fixes, scheduled checkpoints, and a rollback plan.
- Commercial Safety Net (Level 2/3): limited-time credit or tiered discount tied to adoption targets. Documented in an MSA addendum or SOW amendment template.
- Executive Alignment & Roadmap Commitment (Level 3): Exec-to-exec meeting with a concrete deliverable and timeline (e.g., product work scheduled into the next roadmap cycle).
- Short-term Pilot Expansion (save play): Offer an additional seat or module free for 90 days to restore value quickly and buy time for long-term fixes.

Communication templates

- Initial Watch Email (CSM -> Customer)
  Subject: Quick check-in and adoption plan for renewal success
  Body: Hi [Name], we noticed usage in [Module X] has dipped. We recommend a short adoption workshop to identify blockers and a 30-day plan. Suggested times: [range].

- 48-hour Escalation Summary (to internal stakeholders)
  Subject: [Customer] — Level 2 Concern 
  Body: TL;DR: trigger(s), immediate risks, actions taken, blockers, requested owner action (SE ETA, AM commercial runway). Attach: latest health snapshot and QBR notes.

- Exec Brief Template (Level 3)
  - One-line summary of situation
  - Key metrics (health score, usage trends, open bugs)
  - Customer asks and sentiment summary
  - Proposed remediation + commercial offer
  - Decision required from exec (e.g., approve credit up to $X, commit product priority)

Operational runbooks and tracking

- Renewal Runbook: a living doc per account with ladder level, triggers timeline, play attachments, and owner checklist. Link the runbook to the renewal tracker (JIRA or sheet) so that changes update the central dashboard.
- Daily cadence for Level 3: 15-min standup, 30-min technical sync, 1-hr exec brief (as needed).
- Evidence artifacts: meeting notes, health dashboards (export CSV), SE ticket IDs, signed commercial addenda.

Scorecard and metrics to monitor

- Leading indicators: module adoption %, number of active users in critical workflows, time-to-first-success after enablement, open bug count severity >= P2.
- Lagging indicators: NRR, churn, renewal outcome.
- Operational KPIs: mean time to ladder upgrade/downgrade, % of escalations resolved within SLA, % of Level 3 cases with Exec Sponsor assigned within 24 hours.

Decision matrix (quick reference)

- If health_score >= 85 -> Level 0 (no action beyond QBR)
- If 65 <= health_score < 85 AND decline_in_usage > 10% -> Level 1 -> run Adoption Jumpstart within 14 days
- If 45 <= health_score < 65 OR rollout_missed_milestone -> Level 2 -> convene SE + AM within 48 hours and propose Commercial Safety Net if remediation ETA > 2 weeks
- If health_score < 45 OR customer expresses non-renewal intent -> Level 3 -> Escalation Lead + Exec Sponsor in 24 hours

Sample scenario (fictional)

- Acme Media — 75 days to renewal
  - Signal: Health score 68, weekly active users down 22%, two stalled integrations.
  - Ladder: Level 1 -> escalated to Level 2 after 10 days when a critical integration ticket timed out.
  - Response: SE led hotfix sprint, AM drafted a targeted 3-month credit tied to usage recovery, Escalation Lead put daily checkpoints. Outcome: renewed with a 6-month staged rollout and tracked adoption goals.

Checklists (quick-action)

- On Level 1: run adoption workshop, update runbook, schedule QBR refresh, attach usage targets.
- On Level 2: open SE ticket, confirm ETA, draft commercial safety net, set 48-hour internal checkpoint.
- On Level 3: create Save Squad, schedule exec meeting, prepare commercial term sheet, notify Legal for accelerated review.

How to use this doc in a QBR

- Add the ladder snapshot as a one-slide insert in the QBR: current rung, last 90-day movement, active plays, and next 30-day asks. Use the slide to align execs to a single decision.

Notes and open questions

- Standardize health score calculation across product teams (current score components vary by module). Owner: Data Ops.
- Fast-track legal approval thresholds for credits to reduce time-to-offer; propose a pre-approved credit band for Escalation Leads. Owner: Legal + Finance.

Attachments to create (templated artifacts)

- Adoption workshop agenda (template)
- 48-hour escalation summary template (internal)
- Exec brief one-pager (slide)
- Contract addendum template for commercial safety net

References

- Link to renewal tracker (JIRA board): JIRA-CS-789
- Confluence: Customer Health Runbook (CONFLUENCE-1234)

Ownership and next steps

- Draft to review with CS leadership: Priya Desai
- Pilot with three at-risk accounts in Q1: owners assigned (list in linked tracker)
- Feedback loop: capture play effectiveness in the renewal tracker and iterate quarter-over-quarter.

End of document
